differences_that_matter_here: push records: the run's code writes one push record per attempt, after the POST, carrying status sent or failed; main writes a push record fsynced before the POST and a push_result record after it. The run's alerts.jsonl therefore has push records with status and no push_result records.
rate-limit probe: in the run's code a failed or rate-limited first chunk did not stop the sweep's fan-out; main stops it. No chunk failed in this run.
plan: the run's plan counts the first minute as the daily-bar passes plus the average sweep rate (108); main counts both passes plus a whole first sweep (118). Both stay under the 500 cap.

start-up: main checks a stop request and its 600 s start-up deadline before every start-up request and wait (watch.py at 1b8d63349e5c: line 65, checkpoint at 637-641, nap at 643-646), and refuses an --out inside a git worktree (line 915). The run's code (dca569ae) applied its 600 s deadline (line 60) only inside the daily-bar passes' budget waits and retries (load_bars, lines 282 and 289), checked for a stop only before the start-up began (line 569), and did not refuse an --out inside a worktree.

limitations: Data-only watch: it evaluates no strategy and qualifies no gate. The tiers are unvalidated monitoring thresholds.
BOATS is one ATS, so its volume is indicative venue data, not consolidated volume. The fund tag misses some ETFs.

The code is not on main: the run commit dca569ae is in no local ref (remote-tracking branches included) and not in the history of refs/pull/480/head. Its watch.py is the same blob as 6545d7ad in that history, and main's version differs (code.main_version).

The journal holds no exit line and the transient unit is gone from the service manager, so the exit status and the unit's result are not recorded; the watch's stop record says stop_time with no error. Whether any stop at 04:05 ET was configured is not recorded either.
The watch's own files do not record the key file; the unit's ExecStart names the $PAPER_ENV_FILE pointer (account 1), not its value.
What created the output directory is not recorded: it was born 50 ms before the unit's Started record, and the watch's own mkdir found it in place.
No broker read covers the watch window on account 1; the no-order statement rests on the code and the recorded calls.
Posts are recorded as sent when the POST returned without an error; delivery was not checked.
The first sweep came 130.0 minutes after the session opened at 20:00 ET. The session bar's volume is cumulative, so the first sweep's alerts include activity from before the watch started.
Each sweep returned 9,669 of the 9,683 watched names, with the same per-chunk counts in all 176 sweeps; which 14 names were missing is not recorded.
evidence_note: Built from the private watch outputs (start.json, stop.json, sweeps.jsonl, alerts.jsonl, top.jsonl, board.json and the snapshot files, read-only), the unit's records in the systemd user journal, systemctl --user show, git objects of the run commit and of main, a scratch clone of refs/pull/480/head fetched into a scratch directory on 2026-09-30, filesystem metadata, and the private series freeze notes (cited by sha256). Figures present in two or more sources were cross-checked by assertion, and a mismatch stops the build. Other fields come from one source; field_provenance names them. No credential, account id, account number, account fingerprint, pid, invocation id or host path is recorded.
